findings.title: R5-R3 evidence manifests do not verify against the binding tree
findings.requirement: Qualification plan section 11 and QD3Q-08; commission section 9
findings.observation: The top-level R5-R3 manifest has 47 entries: 19 match the committed Git blobs, 27 match only the CRLF working tree, and 1 (evidence/fixtures.json) is stale. The evidence-level manifest has 31 entries: 2 match Git blobs, 27 match only the working tree, 1 is stale (fixtures.json), and the manifest self-reference is not a content digest. The manifest hashes CRLF working-tree bytes, so a clean LF checkout fails it. evidence/fixtures.json was changed after the manifest was generated by commit 44085d3 (post-R5-R3), invalidating the signed digest.
findings.reproducer: For each manifest line, SHA-256 the committed blob (git cat-file blob) and the working-tree file, and compare with the recorded digest.
findings.effect: The R5-R3 evidence chain is not verifiable as signed, and the R5-R4 claim that R5-R3 records are unchanged is inaccurate. This is an evidence-integrity failure under the disposition rule C.

findings.title: The differential D3 native bridge is not the shipped D3 native bridge
findings.requirement: Commission sections 3, 8 and 9; qualification plan section 9
findings.observation: build-bridge.sh rewrites native/dogwoodsharp-bridge/Cargo.toml to depend on the patched corrected-reference dogwood-language tree, then regenerates the lock. The shipped/regression bridge is built by eng/Build-Native.ps1 from the upstream git dependency and the committed lock ec901557. Recorded differential bridge hashes are linux 4b6c3409 and osx-arm64 73d29a70; the Windows differential native was not preserved. Shipped hashes are linux 39afbfd0, osx-arm64 fbd2e98a and win-x64 78f64c4b (a separate local shipped build produced 94811767). The hosted six-cell cells therefore exercise a qualification-only native, not the shipped artifact.
findings.effect: Hosted Linux/macOS evidence does not bind to the production native asset. A Windows control with the shipped bridge still passes 124/124 and is semantically identical, and the independent six-cell package-consumer matrix passes with the shipped natives, which bounds the behavioral risk but does not cure the provenance defect in the differential evidence.

findings.title: The D3 bridge dependency graph is regenerated and not pinned
findings.requirement: Qualification plan section 9 (locked graphs) and section 11
findings.observation: build-bridge.sh deletes/regenerates the lock and pins only cedar-policy-core. An independent rebuild resolved 36 newer packages than the committed lock (for example jiff 0.2.46 to 1.0.3, regex 1.13.1 to 1.13.2), producing lock d07dc3fb instead of committed ec901557 and bridge 620dca4a. Only a lock hash is recorded; the generated lock text is not preserved. Separately, three Windows shipped builds from the same committed lock produced three different image hashes (4f0bd32a, 78f64c4b, 94811767), so the native binary is not byte-reproducible across environments either.
findings.effect: The D3 adapter is not built from its committed locked graph, so the execution is not reproducible from the repository. This is a mandatory plan requirement.

findings.title: CedarSharp native provenance is unpinned and not the package native
findings.observation: build-cedarsharp.sh clones jenolaszlo-sketch/cedar-sharp main without a commit (main a25181d at review time). The CedarSharp 1.0.0 package manifest declares sourceCommit 324d3c09fc94ab91464ec340eb81e4b167deb6f5, which the GitHub API reports as not present (HTTP 422). Rebuilt native hashes (linux 9e8800ed, osx-arm64 740e7410) differ from the package natives (linux 85433a35, win-x64 77de6976, osx-arm64 290fcce9).
findings.effect: Hosted Linux/macOS cells do not test the published CedarSharp native. A Windows control with the published 77de6976 native passes 124/124, bounding behavioral risk but leaving the provenance gap.

findings.title: Original OQ-01 case is an unregistered Allow-versus-failure divergence
findings.requirement: Qualification plan sections 5 and 7; commission section 6
findings.observation: Independent re-execution of the single-case OQ-01 fixture reproduces upstream evaluation failure with no decision and D3 Allow. FCN-05 covers TC-03 through TC-06 only, where both sides fail closed; it cannot cover this Allow-versus-failure case. The case has no ED or FCN row in any signed register. The owner contract decision says D3 is correct, but the machine-readable expectation is absent.
findings.effect: An observed authorization divergence is governed by prose alone, contrary to the register requirement. It is outside the 124-case corpus, so it does not change 124/124, but it is an open contract registration gap.

findings.title: Cross-cell fixture byte hashes differ by line ending
findings.observation: Windows evidence records fixturesSha256 B563AD19 (CRLF working tree); hosted evidence records 568267E0 (LF committed blob). The JSON content is identical and the classifications match.
findings.effect: Semantic fixture identity is established by content; byte identity is not. Record the canonical LF blob hash and avoid CRLF manifests.

findings.title: Harness self-test is skipped on Linux and macOS
findings.observation: self-test.sh exits 0 with 'Original oracle not available on non-Windows' for Linux/macOS. The independent Windows run executed all 19 self-test controls successfully on both TFMs.
findings.effect: Negative-control coverage is established on Windows only; Linux/macOS cells do not execute the harness meta-tests.

findings.title: Representation-invariance test-count claim is inaccurate
findings.observation: The R5-R3/R5-R4 records claim 40 representation-invariance tests. The committed class contains 16 xUnit cases per TFM (96 total in the CedarSharp test project per TFM, 71 core tests per TFM). All pass on net8.0 and net10.0.
findings.effect: The campaign is valid but the stated count is not reproducible; report measured counts.

findings.title: D2 bridge identity is hardcoded, not compiler-attested
findings.observation: native/dogwoodsharp-bridge/src/lib.rs returns literal cedarVersion 4.11.0 and rustVersion 1.99.1. Cargo's rust-version is a minimum, not an exact pin. Unlike the CedarSharp native (build.rs stamps the compiler), a different rustc would still be reported as 1.99.1.
findings.effect: The DogwoodSharp identity gate proves compatibility values, not the compiler that produced the D2 bridge.

findings.title: R5-R3 historical tooling and fixtures were modified in place
findings.observation: Commit 44085d3 rewrote docs/reviews/d3-impl-01-r5-r3/evidence/fixtures.json after the R5-R3 manifest was generated. Commit 17d90b8 changed the R5-R3 probe source to add the macOS dladdr path. The R5-R4 handoff says R5-R3 records are unchanged and the manifest is untouched; the manifest is untouched but no longer covers the content.
findings.effect: Combined with Q3-F01, this is a preservation and evidence-integrity failure.
